title: Field Installation and Runtime Tuning: Operator Handbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This operator handbook documents the recommended field installation steps and runtime tuning knobs for Redwood private/on‑prem inference deployments. It is intended for field engineers, SREs, and customer operators who perform initial installs and run long‑term production workloads. The guidance below balances application SLOs (latency, throughput), hardware reliability, and predictable cost.

Scope: Applies to VPC-connected and air‑gapped on‑prem nodes running the Redwood inference runtime (rwd-runtime v2.x) on NVIDIA Ampere/Grace Hopper GPUs and x86_64 CPU hosts. Does NOT replace customer change control; follow local maintenance windows and CAB processes.

Owner and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (runtime field ops)
- Oncall escalation: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
- Field engineering lead: Maya Chen (author)

Key SLOs and operational thresholds

- P99 single‑request latency: <= 350 ms (for model family: small-medium sequences)
- P95 throughput stability: <= 5% variance over 15m window for steady load profiles
- GPU memory pressure alert threshold: 85% sustained for >2m -> trigger eviction workflow
- Node temperature: warning at 75°C, critical at 85°C measured at GPU die sensor
- KV cache warmup target: 70% effective cache hit rate within 10 minutes of traffic ramp

Pre-installation checklist (operator tasks)

1) Verify hardware compatibility and firmware
   - Confirm GPU driver: NVIDIA driver 545.x or later (verify with nvidia-smi).
   - Confirm CUDA toolkit: 12.1 compatible (for runtime kernels).
   - Base OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (kernel 5.15+) or RHEL 9.x with approved backports.
   - BMC & BIOS firmware: vendor recommended baseline; toggles for SR‑IOV/VT-d applied where required.

2) Network and security prechecks
   - Validate MTU across path: recommended 9000 for high throughput interconnects.
   - Verify TLS inspection bypass for control plane endpoints in pilot installs.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM reachability if using customer key material; ensure ports 443 (API) and 8200 (vault) as applicable.

3) Capacity planning quick validation
   - Verify GPU / CPU inventory and labeling: use rwd-inventory-agent --list to assert device IDs.
   - Sanity check disk latency for model shards: read 95th percentile < 5ms for p95 baseline.

Configuration table (minimum recommended settings)

| Area | Setting | Example / Command | Purpose |
|------|---------|-------------------|---------|
| Kernel | vm.swappiness | 10 | reduce swapping for low-latency workloads |
| CPU | intel_pstate | performance (or set governor to performance) | avoid CPU C‑state latencies |
| HugePages | vm.nr_hugepages | 128 per node (adjust to model size) | reduce TLB pressure for large memory maps |
| Network | net.core.rmem_max / wmem_max | 4194304 | adequate socket buffers for high throughput |
| RDMA | mlx5_core params | enable if present | low-latency transport for multi‑host KV cache sync |

Note: when configuring hugepages, coordinate with container runtimes and CRI OOM reservations.

Step-by-step field install (operator playbook)

A. Base OS and bootstrap
1. Apply OS image and baseline packages: apt-get update && apt-get install -y qemu-kvm docker.io kubelet
2. Disable swap: sudo swapoff -a and remove swap entries from /etc/fstab (Redwood runtime expects swap disabled)
3. Apply sysctl settings from /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood.conf (example below)

# /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood.conf
vm.swappiness=10
vm.nr_hugepages=128
net.core.rmem_max=4194304
net.core.wmem_max=4194304
fs.file-max=2097152

B. GPU driver and container runtime
1. Install NVIDIA driver and OCI runtime: follow vendor guide for driver 545.x and nvidia-container-toolkit. Verify: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
2. Configure container runtime to use GPU devices and set rwd-runtime container limits: devices: all, memory: host-mapped for model-shard caches.

C. Kubernetes / Orchestration specifics (if applicable)
1. Node taints and labels: label nodes with redwood/role=serving and taint redwood=reserve:NoExecute until ready.
2. Kubelet tuning: --eviction-hard=memory.available<250Mi,nodefs.available<1% --system-reserved=cpu=800m,memory=2Gi --kube-reserved=cpu=500m,memory=1Gi
3. Admission policy: enable auto‑inject of rwd-sidecar for telemetry and graceful shutdown hooks.

Runtime tuning: live knobs and when to change them

- KV cache sizing and eviction policy
  - Default: LRU with per‑tenant soft limit at 70% memory.
  - If you see P99 tail latency spikes correlated with cache pressure, reduce per‑tenant prefetch factor and increase background eviction frequency: set RUNTIME_KVCACHE_EVICT_INTERVAL=30s.
- Batching parameters
  - Default: adaptive batching with max_batch_size=48 and latency_target_ms=80.
  - For latency‑sensitive endpoints reduce max_batch_size to 8 and set latency_target_ms=30.
- Quantization fallback rules
  - Use int8 quantized model variants for low‑cost, fallback to fp16 for quality regressions. Configure via model manifest: "fallback_policy": "quality-first" or "cost-first".

Telemetry and acceptance criteria (post-installation)

Acceptance test suite (automated post-install checks):
1) Latency smoke: run load generator (rwd-loadgen) with 50 concurrent clients for 5 minutes; confirm P99 < SLO and error rate < 0.5%.
2) KV cache warmup: replay 10k representative requests; hit rate >= 70% within 10 minutes.
3) Model load and swap: load 3 model variants under realistic memory constraints; no OOM/killer events.
4) Telemetry sampling: ensure 1% full traces, 10% token‑level stats, 100% error logs; verify ingestion into Redwood Console endpoint.

Example acceptance commands
# run smoke latency test
rwd-loadgen --target-endpoint https://local-rwd:8443 --concurrency 50 --duration 300

# check GPU memory pressure
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 5

Upgrade and rollback procedures (safe path)

Principles: always keep a warm rollback artifact; perform upgrades during low traffic windows; canary first then progressive rollout.

Sequence (recommended):
1) Canary: deploy runtime image rwd-runtime:v2.7-canary to 5% of serving nodes; monitor for 30 minutes. Key metrics: P99 latency, error rate, KV cache hit rate, memory headroom.
2) Progressive rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15–30 minute observation windows. If any window breaches SLOs, trigger automatic partial rollback for the last cohort.
3) Full rollback: if canary or early rollout fails, execute forced rollback to rwd-runtime:v2.6 with the following command (example for k8s):

kubectl set image ds/rwd-runtime rwd-runtime=registry.redwood.ai/rwd-runtime:v2.6 --namespace serving

Rollback checklist: preserve /var/lib/rwd/kvcache snapshot (if available), preserve model shard pointers, and restore model manifest versions.

Incident handling and known failure modes

- Symptom: gradual P99 latency increase with CPU steal
  - Likely cause: noisy neighbor or background processes. Action: isolate processes (systemctl stop backup.service); move noisy pods to dedicated nodes.
- Symptom: rapid memory growth and OOM
  - Likely cause: model shard leak during swap. Action: restart runtime container for affected tenant and increase OOM guard (cgroup memory.high).
- Symptom: KV cache desync after node reboot
  - Likely cause: stale index; Action: trigger rwd-kv-reindex --node <id> and warm traffic through warmed nodes only.

Diagnostics commands and quick references

- rwd-status --full : show runtime health, model versions, cache hit rates
- rwd-telemetry tail --service serving : stream last 100 telemetry events
- rwd-kv-stats --tenant <tenant_id> : per-tenant cache stats
- nvidia-smi topo --matrix : verify PCIe/NVLink topology for multi‑GPU nodes

Operational runbook snippets (for oncall)

1) P99 latency breach (SLO > threshold)
  - Immediately: mark incident and increase sampling to 100% for traces.
  - 0–10m: identify change in traffic pattern using rwd-telemetry queries; check recent deploys.
  - 10–30m: if cannot mitigate with scaling / tuning, rollback last runtime/model change for affected cohort.
  - Owner: site‑ops engineer and runtime oncall.

2) Persistent GPU overheating
  - Immediately: throttle workloads (set node taint redwood=thermal:NoSchedule) and alert hardware vendor.
  - 30–60m: verify fan curves and server room HVAC; collect GPU die temps and GPU power draw logs.

Appendices

A. Example model manifest snippet (quantization + fallback)
{
  "model": "redwood-7b-q8",
  "variants": [
    {"name": "q8", "quant": "int8", "memory_mb": "24576"},
    {"name": "fp16", "quant": "fp16", "memory_mb": "51200"}
  ],
  "fallback_policy": "cost-first",
  "kvcache": {"soft_limit_mb": 20000, "evict_interval_s": 30}
}

B. Troubleshooting checklist (quick)

- Confirm kernel and driver versions (nvidia-smi, uname -r)
- Check disk latency and inode usage (ioping, iostat)
- Confirm kubelet evictions and system reserved (journalctl -u kubelet)
